title: Understanding PCA
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It is often used to make data easy to explore and visualize.

title: PCA and Variance
text: PCA works by identifying the directions (principal components) in which the variance of the data is maximized. The first principal component is the direction of maximum variance.

title: SVD and PCA
text: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is a mathematical technique that can be used to perform PCA. The SVD of a matrix decomposes it into three other matrices, U, Σ, and V.

title: Computing Variance in PC1 Direction
text: To compute the variance of the data in the PC1 direction using the U and V matrices from SVD, you need to consider the singular values in Σ. The variance in the PC1 direction is given by the square of the first singular value.
